title: Grateful Dead Live at Davis Gymnasium on 1971-04-14
source: 16/48kHz: 7 Inch 1/4 Track Reel Master @ 7.5 ips (Recorded By Bob Mathews); Transferred By Dick Latvala(Master Reel Playback on a Technics 1506 Reel to Reel-Sony PCM-R500 DAT Deck @ 48KHz); DAT x ONE play back on a Sony PCM R-500-Digital Audio Labs Card deluxe-WAV @ 16/48KHz; Editing (Adobe Audition CC)-Mastering & Processing (iZotope Ozone 6)-FLAC encoding(dBpoweramp)- Tagging(Tag & Re-name)

ai_review.summary: Superb soundboard capture (with occasional hum) of a scorching Pennsylvania ’71 show, highlighted by a blazing China Cat solo, funky Rider, expansive Bird Song and killer Sugar Magnolia.
ai_review.review: The performance is described as one of the best the Dead ever played in Pennsylvania, with high‑energy first‑set numbers and a second set that builds from an extended Bird Song into a funk‑charged Rider and a spectacular Sugar Magnolia. The soundboard recording is overall superb despite some static, low‑frequency hum and inaudible keyboards, and it isolates solos (Bobby and Jerry) beautifully.

ai_rating.rationale: Both reviewers gave 5 stars and praise the musical performance heavily; recording issues are minor, leading to a high combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Overall superb sound with occasional static, distortion and low‑frequency hum typical of early ’71 tapes; keyboards largely buried, giving room for audience bleed, but solos are well isolated.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set builds strong energy, ending with Second That Emotion and Casey Jones; second set opens with a long Bird Song, followed by an engaging mix of funkier Rider and a guiro‑enhanced Sugar Magnolia, with the rest flowing naturally.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Uses crybaby pedal on Sugar Magnolia, provides lead lines in Bird Song; solo on China Cat noted as perfunctory but mix isolates him well.
band_member_comments.Phil: Ron "Pig" McKernan’s keyboards are mostly inaudible, limiting his presence to a few vocal contributions and brief tuning bits.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bobby's solo in China Cat is described as a bona fide, riff‑laden performance that drives the band; his funkiness shines on Rider.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann locks into a funky groove on Rider and maintains tight drumming throughout; overall drum work noted as tight (Johnny B. Good).
